topIssues.title: op-supernode: Prevent local-safe promotion while verified state is stale
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
**Claude:** I found this during the interop implementation review.

An L1 reorg can leave `verifiedDB` ahead of local-safe. During this window, unverified local-safe blocks can receive the safe label.

Event sequence:

1. `verifiedDB` records old-branch block `Y[N]` and its L1 inclusion (`interop.go:597-606`).
2. An L1 reorg resets local-safe to common ancestor `M`, where `M < N` (`engine/events.go:117-128`).
3. The next interop round requests timestamp `N+1` (`interop.go:597-606`).
4. `checkChainsReady` calls `OptimisticAt(N+1)` on every chain (`interop.go:1146-1166`).
5. The target exceeds local-safe, so `LocalSafeBlockAtTimestamp` returns `ethereum.NotFound` (`chain_container.go:559-580`).
6. `observeRound` returns on that error before checking `Y[N]`'s L1 inclusion (`interop.go:620-640`). No database rewind starts.
7. Derivation advances the new canonical branch to `X[K]`, where `M < K < N`.
8. `SafeL2Head` still receives stale verified block `Y[N]` (`engine_controller.go:227-247`).
9. Because `N > K`, `resolveVerifiedAsSafe` returns `X[K]` directly (`engine_controller.go:245-247`).
10. This return bypasses the verified hash checks at `engine_controller.go:249-264`.
11. The next forkchoice update supplies `X[K]` as `SafeBlockHash` (`engine_controller.go:670-686`).
12. Once every chain reaches `N+1`, the L1 check runs and the verified database rewinds.

`X[K]` is canonical and local-safe. It has not passed cross-chain verification, so it must not receive the cross-safe label.

Expected behavior:

- Check accepted L1 consistency even when the next frontier is not ready.
- Never promote local-safe solely because the recorded verified head is ahead.
- Fall back to a canonical verified ancestor, the cross-safe cache, or finalized state.

topIssues.title: kona-sp1: revm-precompile 42 pulls sha2 0.11, which has no SP1 patch
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
## Situation

revm-precompile 42 (pulled in by reth v2.5.0, #22495) depends on `sha2 = "0.11"`. The SP1 guest workspace accelerates SHA-256 by patching `sha2` with [sp1-patches/RustCrypto-hashes](https://github.com/sp1-patches/RustCrypto-hashes), and a `[patch.crates-io]` entry only replaces the version it names: the guest patches [`sha2 0.10.9`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/2191ce5dd2569534fb3016f7a931eabc78cc6f8c/rust/kona/sp1/programs/Cargo.toml#L137). sp1-patches has no `patch-sha2-0.11.*` tag (only mirrors of the upstream `sha2-v0.11.0-*` tags), and Succinct's own zkevm still pins patched 0.10.9.

So the guest now carries two `sha2` crates: patched 0.10.9 (alloy, kona) and vanilla 0.11.0, whose only dependent is revm-precompile. Two consensus paths hash through the vanilla copy inside the zkVM: the SHA-256 precompile (0x02) and the KZG point-evaluation versioned-hash check. Correctness is unaffected; those hashes run as plain RISC-V cycles instead of the SHA-256 syscalls, i.e. a proving-cost regression. `check-sp1-guest-precompile-patches` caught it.

## Workaround in #22495

revm 42 routes both hashes through its pluggable `Crypto` trait, so kona's `CustomCrypto` now [implements `sha256`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/2191ce5dd2569534fb3016f7a931eabc78cc6f8c/rust/kona/sp1/crates/client/src/precompiles/custom.rs#L24) with the client crate's own `sha2`, which is the patched 0.10 line in the guest. The vanilla 0.11 stays compiled in as dead code (`DefaultCrypto`), so the CI check gained an [exemption](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/2191ce5dd2569534fb3016f7a931eabc78cc6f8c/rust/justfile#L298-L318): an unpatched `sha2` is tolerated only while revm-precompile is its sole dependent.

Residual risk: the guard checks the dependency graph, not call sites. A future revm-precompile that hashes with `sha2` directly instead of through `Crypto` would regress silently.

## Follow-up

1. **SP1 (Succinct):** publish a `patch-sha2-0.11.0-sp1-6.x` tag in sp1-patches/RustCrypto-hashes. revm-precompile ≥ 42 (revm 42, reth ≥ v2.5.0) requires sha2 0.11, so every SP1 program executing a current revm is affected, not only kona.
2. **Here, once the tag exists:** add `sha2 0.11` to the guest's `[patch.crates-io]`, delete the `CustomCrypto::sha256` override and the check exemption, and restore the strict "every sha2 resolves from sp1-patches" invariant.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Fable 5.1*

topIssues.title: [Tracking] Amsterdam on the OP Stack
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Tracking issue for adopting the Amsterdam EIPs on L2, i.e. the first OP fork whose `OpSpecId` maps to `SpecId::AMSTERDAM`. The L1 side (surviving Glamsterdam on L1 while L2 stays on Fusaka) is #20151 / #22698; this issue collects the L2 adaptations that are known to be needed and has no schedule yet.

## Todo

- [ ] **Deposit gas under EIP-8037.** Upstream splits a transaction's gas into regular gas, capped at 2^24, and a state-gas reservoir. Deposits are exempt from the cap: `OpHandler::tx_gas` gives a deposit its whole gas limit as regular gas and an empty reservoir ([`handler.rs#L211`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/9d41f32cef2b14519349a661fb21fb82b0334e42/rust/op-revm/src/handler.rs#L211)), which is only meaningful while no OP fork enables EIP-8037. Decide whether a deposit gets a reservoir like every other transaction or stays uncapped regular gas, adapt `tx_gas` to that, and decide whether `validate_initial_tx_gas` should skip deposits: it is not overridden and under EIP-8037 checks a deposit's intrinsic and floor gas against the cap ([`handler.rs#L209`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/9d41f32cef2b14519349a661fb21fb82b0334e42/rust/op-revm/src/handler.rs#L209)). `validate_env` is already skipped for deposits. Spec first, then op-revm.
- [ ] **Block gas accounting.** `OpBlockExecutor` tracks a single `gas_used` where upstream tracks regular and state block gas separately and returns `GasOutput::with_state_gas` ([`block/mod.rs#L786`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/9d41f32cef2b14519349a661fb21fb82b0334e42/rust/alloy-op-evm/src/block/mod.rs#L786)); the header and receipt fields for state gas need an L2 decision.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Fable 5.1*

topPRs.title: rust: update reth to v2.5.0 and drop the op-rs fork
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
Moves the reth pin from the OP fork `op-rs/reth@aef8d3ef` back to upstream `paradigmxyz/reth`, `tag = "v2.5.0"`.

**The fork is droppable.** Its branch is upstream `f2eecc65` plus exactly one cherry-pick, `aef8d3ef92 feat(trie): expose payload state root receiver`. That patch is byte-identical (modulo blob hashes and line offsets) to upstream `92cf59e2be`, and `92cf59e2be` is in v2.5.0. `f2eecc65` is an ancestor of v2.5.0. So the fork carries nothing unique and the pin goes back to upstream.

Stacked on #22477 — this branch still contains its two commits, so review only `rust: update reth to v2.5.0 and drop the op-rs fork`.

## Shared versions

Synced to what v2.5.0 pins: `revm` 41.0.0 → 42.0.1 (subcrates 42.0.0), `revm-inspectors` 0.41 → 0.42, `alloy-evm` 0.37.0 → 0.38.0, alloy core 1.6.0 → 1.6.1, the alloy main family 2.1.1 → 2.3.0, published reth-core crates 0.5.0 → 0.6.0. All four lockfiles refreshed; no unrelated git-source drift.

## Upstream churn worth reviewing closely

**revm 41 → 42 is a major, not a routine bump.** It reworks the whole `Handler` gas pipeline around `GasTracker` and the EIP-2780 runtime gas phase, so `OpHandler::last_frame_result` is a genuine re-derivation, not a signature patch. The new body settles the frame with upstream's `handle_reservoir_remaining_gas` and applies the pre-Regolith deposit rules on top of the settled result; the EIP-8037 create refund is now upstream's `FrameResult::refundable_state_gas`, which reads a recorded `charged_create_state_gas` flag instead of inferring the condition.

**A mirror had genuinely drifted.** op-revm's `ExecuteEvm::replay` is a `copy` of upstream's `Evm` impl; upstream added an error path that finalizes the journal so a failed transaction does not leak into the next one, and our copy did not have it. Same class as the SDM warm-set leak (#21723). Fixed.

**Trie: `wiped` no longer derived from account status.** reth's `HashedStorage::from_bundle_state` stopped setting it (paradigmxyz/reth#26524); `HashedPostStateProvider::hashed_post_state` now owns destroyed-account handling and returns `ProviderResult`. Two OP consequences:
- `isthmus::withdrawals_root` builds its `HashedStorage` directly from the `BundleState`, bypassing `hashed_post_state`, so it keeps propagating `wiped` explicitly. Behaviour-preserving; `L2ToL1MessagePasser` is never destroyed in practice, but this is the withdrawals root, so it is preserved rather than dropped.
- `OpProofsStateProviderRef::hashed_post_state` now materializes the zeroed slots against the proofs storage at the parent block, mirroring upstream's `LatestStateProviderRef`.

**Behaviour change to confirm:** `ExecutionWitnessRecord`'s only public exit is now `into_execution_witness`, which also fills in ancestor headers. The payload-builder witness (`debug_executePayload`) therefore gained a headers provider and now returns headers, which it previously left empty. `debug_executionWitness` on the same server already returned them, so this makes the two consistent — but it is a response change, not just an adaptation.

**Flashblock log stream:** `ReceiptConverter` gained `RpcLog`/`convert_log` and the log-matching helpers convert through it. A flashblock is a payload, not a sealed block, so the header handed to the converter carries only the number, hash and timestamp the log fields need — exactly the values the old API took positionally. OP's `convert_log` is the identity.

Smaller compile-forced items: `from_reverts_auto` → `HashedPostStateSorted::from_reverts`, `ChangesetCache` → `reth_storage_overlay::OverlayManager`, `BuiltPayloadExecutedBlock::changed_paths` and `BuildNewPayload::{cache,state_root_handle}` removed, `validate_block_post_execution_with_hashed_state` gained a parent header (unused by OP), `calculate_initial_tx_gas` gained an EIP-2780 argument, `alloy_genesis::ChainConfig` gained `bogota_time`.

**Latent misdeclaration exposed:** kona-proof now declares `ark-bls12-381`'s `scalar_field` feature. It used to arrive by feature unification with revm-precompile, which moved to ark-bls12-381 0.6 — so `ark_bls12_381::Fr` stopped resolving with no change on our side.

## Mirrors

All 24 `UPSTREAM-MIRROR` tags re-verified against v2.5.0 / revm 42 / alloy-evm 0.38: 19 current, 5 frozen, none stale, `just mirrors --check` exits 0. Only two mirrors had actually moved upstream (`revm_handler::api`, `revm_handler::Handler::last_frame_result` — plus the mechanically-forced `refund`); the rest were verified unchanged. The frozen `DatabaseMetrics` port's recorded version moved from `rev:aef8d3e` to `rev:f2eecc6` so it names a commit reachable in the remote we now build against.

Two findings that are **not** fixed here, for a separate decision:
- `op-reth`'s `DEV_HARDFORKS` omits `EthereumHardfork::Osaka`, which upstream's dev list has had since before the old pin. Pre-existing drift, not introduced by this bump.
- That tag's prose claims the list "carries three Glacier forks upstream's does not" — neither list has them. The prose is wrong; left alone to keep this diff to the bump.

## Review (`reth-update-reviewer`)

Run per `.claude/skills/update-reth/SKILL.md`, following `docs/ai/reth-update-review.md`. It surfaced two HIGH findings; I verified both against upstream sources before acting.

**Fixed in the second commit — `MemoryOverlayOpProofsStateProviderRef::hashed_post_state`.** Same paradigmxyz/reth#26524 change as the Isthmus item above, landing in a place the first commit did not cover. Upstream turned `MemoryOverlayStateProviderRef::hashed_post_state` from a bare delegate into one that also zeroes destroyed accounts' slots from the *unpersisted* in-memory blocks; ours stayed a bare delegate, so only the persisted proofs storage got zeroed. Verified by diffing that function at `f2eecc65` (bare delegate) against `v2.5.0` (zeroing loop). It feeds `state_root_with_updates` in the proofs engine, so the symptom is a wrong state root. No compile error, no diff signal — exactly the class this review exists for.

**Reported, not fixed — the SP1 guest lost its patched SHA-256.** revm-precompile 42 moved `sha2` 0.10.9 → 0.11, and `[patch.crates-io]` only replaces the version it names. Verified in `rust/kona/sp1/programs/Cargo.lock`: before, only patched `sha2 0.10.9`; after, that **plus** an unpatched `sha2 0.11.0` whose sole consumer is `revm-precompile 42.0.1`. The SHA-256 precompile and the KZG versioned-hash check now run unaccelerated in the zkVM guest — a proving-cost regression, not a correctness one. The fix is a second patch entry, but only if `sp1-patches` publishes a sha2-0.11 tag; I have not confirmed one exists, so this needs an owner rather than a guess.

The reviewer also raised a set of medium/low items I did **not** act on — they are either pre-existing, inert today, or outside a dependency bump's scope. Listing them so they are not lost: engine persistence defaults moved upstream with no op-side override; kona's in-VM bn254 `ecAdd`/`ecMul` backend moved to ark 0.6; `ark-ff`'s `asm` feature lost the same way `scalar_field` was; c-kzg 2.1.7 → 2.1.8 under kona-host with the SP1 guest left on 2.1.7; `ChainConfig`'s new `bogota_time` absorbed by `..Default::default()` in superchain conversion; `OpSpecId::into_eth_spec` having no Amsterdam arm, so a future one-line edit would switch on EIP-2780 wholesale; and `eth_getMultiProof` arriving as a defaulted trait method on the OP namespace. Each wants its own issue rather than a rider on this PR.

On the deposit gas-cap exemption specifically, the reviewer disagreed with my "nothing changed" and was right to: revm 42 moved `initial_gas_and_reservoir` out of `Handler::execution` into a **new defaulted `Handler::tx_gas`** that op-revm does not override. The call site moved; it still reads `cfg().tx_gas_limit_cap()` and still runs inside the exemption window, so the behaviour holds — but it held by luck of a defaulted method landing inside the window, not by design. That is what the new tests pin.

## Verification

Run locally, exit codes observed:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo check --workspace --tests` (main) | 0 |
| `cargo check --workspace --tests` (op-rbuilder) | 0 |
| `cargo check --workspace --tests` (rollup-boost) | 0 |
| `just fmt-check` | 0 |
| `just lint` (fmt + clippy + docs + mirrors) | 0 |
| `cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features` | 0 — 2904/2904 passed, 11 skipped |
| `just test-docs` | 0 |
| `just check-no-std` | 0 |

The unit-test total is two runs: 2805 with `kona-sp1-proposer` excluded, then its 99 tests alone at `--test-threads 1`. Together they cover the same set; splitting was needed only because this box OOMs on the combined run.

Not run locally: op-reth E2E / acceptance suites, and anything needing a devnet.

## Judgement calls a human should confirm

0. **The SP1 sha2 patch loss above** — highest-consequence unfixed item; needs someone who knows whether an sp1-patches sha2-0.11 tag exists.
1. The `debug_executePayload` witness now includes ancestor headers (see above).
2. `isthmus::withdrawals_root` preserving `wiped` by hand rather than following upstream's zero-slots approach — the fail-safe reading, but it is a deliberate divergence from how upstream now expresses the same thing.
3. `OpBuilder::witness` / `OpPayloadBuilder::payload_witness` gained a headers-provider parameter and a `HeaderProvider` bound. Public API churn in op-reth.
4. `flashblock_receipts_stream` gained `BlockHeader = Header, Receipt = OpReceipt` bounds and yields `RpcLog<Rpc::Network>` instead of `Log` (identical for OP). It has no in-tree callers.
5. The SP1 guest workspace's declared `revm`/`alloy` versions were bumped too. `rust/UPDATING-RETH.md` only tells you to refresh its lockfile, so those declarations had been lagging silently.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Opus 5*

topPRs.title: kona-sp1-proposer: reject pending game ancestry
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
Known pending parents now make cached descendants ineligible for proving or extension, while unknown historical cache gaps retain the existing fail-open behavior. Stale pending branches are tombstoned and cleared atomically; if one is later promoted to the registry anchor, the proposer performs a bounded in-cycle factory rescan against the same pinned L1 view before planning work.

Regression coverage includes pending ancestry, stale eviction, same-index reorg replacement, and anchor recovery. All 253 `kona-sp1-proposer` tests, nightly Rustfmt, and proposer-local Clippy pass; workspace-wide lint was not completed because the fresh worktree lacks the `superchain-registry` submodule and dependency-inclusive Clippy encounters a pre-existing `kona-derive` warning.

Related: #22787

topPRs.title: op-service/log: own the Logger and its slog implementation
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
`op-service/log` now owns its `Logger`: an immutable interface with upstream go-ethereum's method set, minus `Write`, plus `WithContext`, `LogAttrs` and the `*Context` methods. It is backed by our own slog implementation. `op-service/log`, `logfilter` and `testlog` compile and pass their tests against upstream go-ethereum with the `replace` dropped. Before this, they depended on op-geth's logger methods and would break at the cutover.

Output is byte-identical to geth's logger for the terminal, logfmt and JSON handlers, which a differential test pins. Level filtering, the `!BADKEY` handling of an odd argument and `Crit` exiting match op-geth. Two things change on purpose, both to simplify:
- op-geth's mutable `SetContext` is replaced by `WithContext(ctx) Logger`, which returns a derived logger. Every call site already derived a fresh logger and then set its context, so each becomes one call.
- Every method attributes records to its direct caller. `Write`/`WriteCtx` no longer attribute to the caller's caller, and they are gone from our `Logger` because `Log` covers them.

`testlog` now honours the context; its `SetContext` used to be a no-op. So records from devtest and acceptance-test loggers now carry `scope=…` (and `chainID=…` where set), and context-based logfilter rules apply to them. The set of shown and muted lines doesn't change, because the only rule installed in-tree filters by level.

Our `With`/`New` return our `Logger`, so it can't satisfy geth's `log.Logger` directly, because Go has no covariant return types. `ToGeth` converts a logger for the one go-ethereum API that takes one (discv5 in op-node). `SetDefault` also installs our logger as geth's global logger, so geth code running in-process logs through it. Returning geth's `log.Logger` from `With` instead would break 200+ call sites against upstream. The geth view keeps geth's `Write` semantics so that geth's own `log.Info` still attributes records to the geth call site. Handlers and level helpers stay re-exported from go-ethereum, since they exist upstream. `geth.go` is the only file allowed to import it.

Note: logfilter's `TestThreadSafety` races under `-race` because `testlog.CapturingHandler` has no lock. This is pre-existing, reproduces without this PR, and will be fixed in a follow-up.

Stacked on #23017. Part of #22752.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Opus 5.5*

topPRs.title: op-service/log!: make op-service/log a leaf package and the monorepo's logger surface
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
Makes `op-service/log` a leaf package (no in-repo imports) and the logging API that op-service logs through, instead of importing `go-ethereum/log` directly. This is the first step toward owning the log layer before the go-ethereum cutover: once everything logs through `oplog`, the geth-backed names can be swapped for an owned implementation in one place. Being a leaf also lets low-level packages such as `logfilter`, `ioutil` and `tls` import the logger, which the old package's CLI and HTTP dependencies prevented.

No behaviour change. The re-exports are type aliases and variables bound to the geth implementation, not wrappers: a wrapper would shift geth's source-location attribution to `logger.go` (pinned by `logger_test.go`). Migrated and unmigrated packages therefore interoperate. Migrated files import `op-service/log` unaliased, as `log`, so most change only their import line. A depguard test keeps the package a leaf. Reviewing commit by commit is easiest: the package split, then the alias surface with the op-service migration. Each commit builds on its own.

BREAKING CHANGE: Go modules importing `op-service/log` must update imports. The CLI helpers move to `op-service/log/logcli`: `CLIFlags`, `CLIFlagsWithCategory`, `CLIConfig`, `ReadCLIConfig`, `DefaultCLIConfig`, `NewLogger`, `NewLogHandler`, `SetGlobalLogHandler`, `SetupDefaults`, `AppOut`, `LevelFlagValue`, `FormatFlagValue`. `NewLoggingMiddleware` moves to `op-service/httputil`. `oplog.NewLogger` still exists but is now go-ethereum's `NewLogger(slog.Handler)`, so a call with the old `(io.Writer, CLIConfig)` signature fails with an argument error and must switch to `logcli.NewLogger`. CLI flags and env vars are unchanged.

Packages outside op-service still import `go-ethereum/log`; they move in a follow-up. Deferred review findings: the §15 status in `docs/ai/opgeth-decoupling.md` gets updated with that follow-up, and the unused `flags.ReadTestConfig` (unused on develop too) is left for a separate cleanup.

Part of #22752.
